arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Malcolm Stewart argued the ban is not a speech restriction.
He stated the provision is viewpoint-neutral on its face.
He claimed it is a valid condition on a federal program.
Mr. Sommer argued the government does not defend the statute's plain language.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: The Supreme Court examines a federal trademark law. The law bars registration of marks deemed scandalous. The government argues this rule is viewpoint-neutral. The challenger argues the rule targets specific viewpoints.
